newsitem.title: USA: Kodak has lower quarter, higher year.
newsitem.headline: Kodak has lower quarter, higher year.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. Thursday reported lower fourth-quarter profits but higher earnings for the year amid continuing strides to improve its costs.
Investors applauded the results, boosting Kodak's stock $4.40 to $85.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The photographic equipment and film giant said it earned $164 million, or 49 cents per share, in the quarter, compared with profits of $275 million, or 80 cents a share, a year earlier.
However, excluding restructuring costs, the loss on the sale of its Office Imaging operations and earnings from discontinued operations, fourth-quarter earnings were $395 million, or $1.19 a share.
Sales for the quarter rose 5 percent to $4.314 billion.

For the year, Kodak earned $1.288 billion, or $3.82 per share, compared with $1.252 billion, or $3.67 a share a year earlier. Excluding restructuring and other costs, its profits in 1996 were $1.519 billion, or $4.50 per share.
Sales for the year rose 7 percent $15.97 billion.
Eastman Kodak Chairman George Fisher said in a statement that the company continues to improve its costs.
The company said it has seen growth in emerging markets, including China, Russia and Eastern Europe, although it did not provide specific figures.

A Kodak spokesman said the company's restructuring shows how it is seeking to improve its cost structure. The restructuring is the result of Kodak's efforts to eliminate redundancies and streamline worldwide operations, he said.
Kodak took a charge of $256 million for after-tax restructuring costs in the fourth quarter. It also recorded an after-tax loss of $252 million for the sale of its Office Imaging business.
